title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II
corePattern: Unlimited Transactions State Machine DP and Greedy Accumulation of Positive Slopes
interviewTips: Ask if multiple transactions can overlap and if same-day buy-sell is allowed - for Stock II holding at most one share, unlimited completed transactions are allowed.
Contrast with Stock I (single transaction): explain why greedy works here but not there due to unlimited transactions decomposing into independent positive segments.
Mention valley-peak vs sum of positive differences are equivalent - be ready to prove splitting [a,b,c] with a<b<c into (b-a)+(c-b)=c-a.
Edge-case tip: handle n<2, strictly decreasing prices (answer 0, never negative), and large n up to 3*10^4 with O(1) space.
Trade-off: DP state machine generalizes to k transactions and cooldown/fee variants, while greedy O(n) is shortest but not extensible.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force Recursion (Try All Buy/Sell Choices)
approaches.intuition: At each day you have a state: holding a stock or not. If not holding you can buy or skip, if holding you can sell or skip. Explore both choices recursively and take the best profit.
approaches.theory: Model as decision tree with state (i, holding). Recurrence: if holding, best = max(prices[i]+F(i+1,False), F(i+1,True)); else best = max(-prices[i]+F(i+1,True), F(i+1,False)). Base case i==n returns 0 if not holding else -inf (invalid to end holding). This enumerates all 2^n action sequences.

timeComplexity.explanation: Two branches per day (take vs skip action), total 2^n paths for n days. Without memoization each state recomputed.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Recursion depth n for call stack, no extra tables.

steps: dfs(0,False): buy at 7 vs skip -> skip better
dfs(1,False): buy at 1 (-1 + future) vs skip -> buy wins
holding path explores sell at 5 (+5), sell at 3, sell at 6, etc.
Best path found: buy 1 sell 5 (+4) + buy 3 sell 6 (+3) = 7

edgeCases: n=0 or n=1 returns 0, no transaction possible
Strictly decreasing e.g. [7,6,4,3,1] returns 0, recursion never picks negative profit over skip
TLE for n>20, only for correctness baseline

approaches.name: Approach 2: Dynamic Programming - Hold and Cash States
approaches.intuition: Maintain two best profits each day: max profit if holding a stock and max profit if not holding (cash). Each day you can transition by buying, selling, or doing nothing.
approaches.theory: Let hold[i] = max profit on day i ending with stock, cash[i] = max profit ending without stock. Transitions: hold[i]=max(hold[i-1], cash[i-1]-prices[i]), cash[i]=max(cash[i-1], hold[i-1]+prices[i]). Init hold[0]=-prices[0], cash[0]=0. Answer cash[n-1]. Only previous day needed, so compress to O(1) space. This is the unlimited-transaction state machine.

timeComplexity.explanation: Single pass over n prices with O(1) transition per day.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only two variables hold and cash; full O(n) table compressed.

edgeCases: Decreasing [5,4,3,2,1]: hold stays negative, cash stays 0
Increasing [1,2,3,4,5]: cash grows each day to 4

approaches.name: Approach 3: Optimal Greedy - Sum All Positive Differences
approaches.intuition: Because you can do unlimited transactions, every upward step is profit you should capture. If price rises from yesterday to today, buy yesterday and sell today. Sum all such rises.
approaches.theory: Any optimal transaction buy at valley l sell at peak r with l<r can be decomposed: prices[r]-prices[l] = sum(prices[k]-prices[k-1]) for k in (l+1..r) where intermediate steps may go up and down. Negative steps would be skipped by splitting into multiple transactions, positive steps kept. Hence total optimum equals sum over i of max(0, prices[i]-prices[i-1]). Greedy is optimal because transactions are independent and have no cost.

timeComplexity.explanation: One linear scan computing adjacent differences.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only profit accumulator and loop index.
